Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

politics noun

public life, the business of the state

also political life, go into politics, enter politics, be in politics, talk politics, political career, political affairs, take part in politics, cursus honorum

classical

Cael. in Cic. Fam. 8.11.3: quod ad rem pūblicam attinet
Traupman 180
M-O s.v. politics

rēs pūblica, reī pūblicae f.

politics, public affairs

Latin has no separate word for politics: it is the business of the state itself. To go into politics is rem pūblicam capessere (Nep. Them. 2.1; M-O) or Traupman’s rem pūblicam inīre; to be in politics, in rē pūblicā versārī (Traupman 22, 180). For “political”, see political.

Other words

  • rēs cīvīlēs, rērum cīvīlium f. pl. — political affairs, public life

    also used · classical · Tac. H. 2.5: cīvīlium rērum perītus (Lewis & Short); Traupman 180

    Public business as against war or private life (Lewis & Short, s.v. cīvīlis).

  • ambitiō, ambitiōnis f. — politics as the pursuit of office: canvassing

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.1: forēnsium rērum labor et ambitiōnis occupātiō; M-O s.v. politics

    The going round for votes, and so the business of seeking office; also ambition and the courting of favour in general (Lewis & Short). Bribery at elections is ambitus (Traupman 178).

Examples

  • quod ad rem pūblicam attinet, in ūnam causam omnis contentiō conlēcta est, dē prōvinciīs

    as far as politics goes, the whole struggle has come down to one question, the provincesCael. in Cic. Fam. 8.11.3

  • nunc agilis fīō et mersor cīvīlibus undīs

    now I turn man of action and plunge into the waves of politicsHor. Ep. 1.1.16

  • prīmus autem gradus fuit capessendae reī pūblicae bellō Corcȳraeō

    the first step of his political career came in the war with CorcyraNep. Them. 2.1

  • Tūne vīs versārī aliquandō in rē pūblicā?

    Do you want to be involved in politics some day?Traupman 22

  • in rē pūblicā versārī

    to take part in politicsTraupman 180

  • cursus honōrum

    a political career (literally, the course of offices)Tac. H. 1.48 (Lewis & Short s.v. inoffēnsus)

See also political, politician, government, party, election.
